target.notes: Detached review worktree at the PR head. Code delta vs main is one line in the shared git() helper plus the expanded regression; the rest is the author report and session-state bookkeeping.

summary: The fix does what it claims. Independently: with the base helper, a linked worktree run under an inherited GIT_COMMON_DIR pointing at a foreign repo resolves its claim store inside that foreign repo; with the one-line fix it resolves to the canonical store. The expanded regression (canonical/linked x GIT_DIR/GIT_COMMON_DIR) fails exactly the two GIT_COMMON_DIR cases against the base helper and passes all four with the fix. Focused suite 55 passed; full root suite 770 passed, 40 skipped, 1 failed in a provisioned checkout, where the one failure is environmental and identical on the base helper. Integration gate, session-state-check and registry-sync-check are clean. Ruff on the changed test is clean and the helper has the identical six baseline findings. Notes only: sibling raw git subprocess calls elsewhere are unscrubbed but do not choose the claim store (f1), and the full-suite totals depend on nested checkouts (f2).

findings.description: Other raw subprocess git calls in the coordination tooling (session_state_io.py recent-commit log and HEAD refresh, session_stop_hook.py, session_claim.py _git) do not go through the scrubbed helper. None of them chooses the claim store, so the stated defect is closed; they would still inherit a foreign GIT_* environment for the mechanical HEAD and log refresh.
findings.evidence: grep of subprocess.run sites in tools/session_state_io.py:667,730, tools/session_stop_hook.py:57,204,304,489, tools/session_claim.py:_git. claims_dir() uses _workspace_common.git(), which is the scrubbed path.
findings.correction: Optional hardening, not required for this patch: route those calls through the shared helper or scrub the same keys. Left unqueued to avoid bundling.

findings.description: Full-suite totals depend on nested checkouts.
